Halcyon’s flagship model had 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal injury to the relevant regulator within 72 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account of known circumstances and impacts. A fatality, serious injury, or active fire presenting an ongoing risk must be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers must provide affected customers with a safety notice within 5 calendar days of learning of an incident that may indicate a product safety risk, and promptly update the notice as material facts emerge.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The maximum allowed failure rate is 5% for any model. Exceeding this limit requires a regulator-approved corrective-action plan and retesting on a regulator-set schedule; exceeding it alone does not automatically prohibit continued sale while the manufacturer follows the plan, unless the regulator determines there is an imminent or serious risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units must include a remote emergency shut-off capability that can place the battery in a safe state, subject to safeguards against unauthorized activation and loss of communications. For units already installed when this standard takes effect, manufacturers must provide a compatible retrofit or equivalent safe-state solution within 6 years, where technically feasible, and must inform owners of any limitations and interim safety measures.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression designed to limit fire propagation and protect occupants and nearby members of the public. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. The manufacturer must notify the relevant regulator and affected customers promptly, explain the basis for the recall, and provide a remedy and instructions for safe handling.

document.section_notes: The S2 final text drops any sales stop: a model above 5% may keep selling indefinitely while following a corrective-action plan, which is the main weakening and favours Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). S5 keeps a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 with no transition, which Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9) would trigger, while S4 delays suppression to 36 months (the minimum safe-looking boundary for Halcyon's cost concern). Per-model results go to customers and regulators but not the public, meeting both red lines.
